The problem: owners lose money to no-shows, slow table turns, and bookkeeping they don't have time for.

The idea: a low-cost tool that handles waitlist, reservations, and simple daily sales/labor summaries on a phone, priced for a restaurant that does $30k/week. Start by building it with 3-5 local restaurants (my parents' place first), measure table turn time and no-show rates, then expand to similar independent restaurants in the South Bay.

Why me: CS degree, web dev and Python skills, and firsthand knowledge of how the restaurant floor works. Next step: a working prototype for my parents' restaurant within 8 weeks.

# Waitlist pilot: terms and stop conditions (draft for parents' review Thursday)

## What the pilot is
- A phone waitlist and reservation tool for restaurants, tested at one restaurant first (ours), then 2-3 other South Bay owners.
- Free for 4 weeks. After that, $50/month only if the owner wants to keep it.

## What we measure (weekly)
- Guests added to the waitlist per service
- Average quoted wait vs. actual seat time (minutes)
- No-show rate on reservations
- Staff minutes spent on the tool per day (target: under 5)

## Staff workload limits
- Staff never have to enter anything twice. The tool runs beside the paper list, not instead of it.
- I handle setup, changes, and fixes. No changes during Friday rush.

## Stop conditions (any one ends the pilot for that restaurant, no questions asked)
- Staff spend more than 10 min/day on it for 2 weeks in a row
- A guest-facing error (wrong wait time, lost name) happens twice in a week
- Owner or parents ask to stop
- A service is missed because of the tool

## Baseline
- Week of pilot start: record paper-list numbers for 1 week before turning anything on.

## Status
- Our restaurant: pilot running (paid $50 in week 14). Numbers to be pulled this week.
- Other owners: intros requested from parents, not yet confirmed.
